title: Nocturne · Op. 15 No. 1
reviewer: Codex; all four Paderewski pages and both staves of every measure visually audited for pitches, accidentals, octaves, chords, ordered attacks, ties, printed small notes and staff crossings, 2026-11-14. Model review, not independent editorial certification. Per-measure decisions and inventory hashes are recorded in data/nocturne_op15_no1_scan_review.json.
scope: Complete 0–74 model-reviewed pitch/attack counterpart, including the opening pickup, printed small notes, tied continuations and engraved staff ownership. All 1,801 attacks are reviewed against the exact Paderewski scan. Automatic pitch evaluation uses the authoritative captured take. The source scan governs rhythm, sustain, voicing, fingering, pedal and expression; these are not graded. This is an unmeasured study, not an engraved critical edition or a musical-quality assessment.
plan_summary: Learn the three quiet opening sentences; secure the ending backwards early. Compare and learn the varied return separately. Acquire the storm as five independent short sections, mapping bass and melody before figuration. Join the cadence, relaunch and Tempo I boundaries, then assemble A, B, A′ and the whole piece. Use independent starts and relaxed short sets; concert tempo is not required.

sections.title: A · Opening sentence
sections.focus: Sing the melody, map the bass and then the triplet accompaniment. Keep long melody notes alive over the moving left hand. Use starts at the pickup, 5 and 7; include the pickup when joining the opening.

sections.title: A · Decorated answer
sections.focus: Learn the little-note lead-ins and their destinations slowly. Compare the bass changes at 12–16 with the opening; sing the line before adding the accompaniment. Start independently at 9 and 13.

sections.title: A · Closing sentence and stillness
sections.focus: Name the chromatic bass route and distinguish 19–20 from 21–22. Preserve the quiet cadence and fermata at 24. Prepare the F-minor entrance mentally before playing it.

sections.title: B · Con fuoco launch
sections.focus: Map each left-hand sweep and landing first. Block the right-hand alternating intervals, then release into short relaxed groups. Coordinate slowly; stop and rest if tense. Loudness and speed are not memory goals.

sections.title: B · First expansion and withdrawal
sections.focus: Extract the melody and bass from the moving texture. Learn the chromatic changes at 29–30, distinguish 31–32 from 33–34, then the descending exit and 6/8 at 36. Do not practise only from 25.

sections.title: B · Relaunch
sections.focus: Compare with 25–28, then recall this occurrence independently. Name the route after 40: it goes into the new sequence, not back to 29.

sections.title: B · New sequential climb
sections.focus: Block the changing harmony and name each bass destination. Isolate the natural signs at 42–44 and restore the upper-staff D naturals at 43; keep the inner movement separate from the bass.

sections.title: B · Dissolving texture and return route
sections.focus: Sing the top voice, map the left-hand figuration, then coordinate in short sets. Isolate the tied melody and the 6/8 at 48. Practise arriving softly at 49 with a fresh tempo and key reset.

sections.title: A′ · Varied return
sections.focus: Compare with 1–8; learn the new arpeggiated entry, seven-note run at 54 and rewritten answer at 55–56 as distinct events. Do not substitute the opening version from habit.

sections.title: A′ · Decorated answer returns
sections.focus: Compare 57–64 with 9–16, including the different lead-in at 57. Learn ornaments as gestures with clear landing notes. Begin from 57 and 61 without a run-up.

sections.title: A′ · Final closing sentence
sections.focus: Compare with 17–22 but name the final route. The small run at 68 contains a tiny repeated E and G-sharp; learn its exact contour before connecting 69–70.

sections.title: Ending · Smorzando and final arpeggios
sections.focus: Learn 73–74 first, including the cross-staff arpeggios, then prepend 71–72 in normal playing order. Let the ending settle; preserve the distinction between the two final harmonies.
